h: Creation, Divine Peace, and the Rectification of Evil
The sequence of creation and the sanctity of Shabbat culminate in the revelation of peace.
The Creation of Darkness and the Making of Peace

p: שֶׁהַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלּוֹ יָשִׂים עָלֵינוּ בְּרָכָה וְשָׁלוֹם".
"May He Whose peace it is place upon us blessing and peace."
כְּתִיב: "יוֹצֵר אוֹר וּבוֹרֵא חֹשֶׁךְ,
It is written: 'Former of light and Creator of darkness,
עֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם וּבוֹרֵא רָע,
Maker of peace and Creator of evil,
אֲנִי ה' עֹשֶׂה כָל אֵלֶּה".
I am Hashem, Who makes all these.'
וְהִנֵּה הֵיפֶךְ אוֹר הוּא חֹשֶׁךְ,
Now behold, the opposite of light is darkness,
וְהֵיפְכוֹ שֶׁל רַע הוּא טוֹב,
and the opposite of evil is good,
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר: "עוֹשֶׂה טוֹב",
and Scripture ought to have said: 'Maker of good';
וּמַה הַלָּשׁוֹן "עֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם וּבוֹרֵא רָע"?
so why use the phrasing 'Maker of peace and Creator of evil'?
גַּם לֹא מָצִינוּ בִּבְרִיאַת מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית בְּרִיאַת רַע;
Furthermore, we do not find during the creation of the world the creation of 'evil';
דְּחֹשֶׁךְ נִזְכַּר עַל כָּל פָּנִים בְּמַאֲמַר בְּרֵאשִׁית,
for darkness is at least mentioned in the utterance of Bereishit,
אֲבָל רַע לֹא נִזְכַּר.
yet evil is not mentioned.
וְכֵן הִקְשָׁה רַבֵּינוּ רַבִּי בֶּער זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּרִמְזֵי תּוֹרָה,
And so our master Rabbi Ber (the Maggid of Mezeritch) of blessed memory questioned in Rimzei Torah:
שֶׁלֹּא נִזְכַּר בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית רַק טוֹב וְטוֹב מְאֹד
that in Creation nothing is mentioned except 'good' and 'very good,'
עַד מַעֲשֵׂה הַחֵטְא,
until the incident of the sin,
דִּכְתִיב: "עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע".
wherein it is written: 'the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil.'
וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה תִּקְּנוּ:
And the Men of the Great Assembly formulated: "
עוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם וּבוֹרֵא אֶת הַכֹּל",
'Maker of peace and Creator of all,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרָכוֹת יא:).
as stated (Berakhot 11b).
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא,
However, the matter is,
דִּבְמַאֲמָר רִאשׁוֹן – בְּרֵאשִׁית נַמֵּי מַאֲמָר הוּא,
that in the first utterance—Bereishit being also an utterance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לב.)
– as stated (Rosh Hashanah 32a)—
כְּתִיב: "תֹּהוּ וָבֹהוּ וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם",
it is written: 'unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep,' (
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ב, ה) אֵלּוּ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים.
(and in the Midrash, Bereishit Rabbah 2:5) these are the deeds of the wicked.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ",
And that is what is written: 'He makes darkness His secret place,'
שֶׁמַּאֲמָר רִאשׁוֹן כְּנֶגֶד כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁהוּא נֶעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן,
for the first utterance corresponds to Keter Elyon which is concealed from every thought,
וּבָזֶה יוּכַל הָאָדָם לִתְעוֹת כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא בַּחֹשֶׁךְ.
and within this a person can err since he is in darkness.
אַךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה,
Yet Israel arose in the Primordial Thought, "
בְּרֵאשִׁית" – בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ רֵאשִׁית;
'Bereishit'—for the sake of Israel who are called 'first';
וּכְשֶׁתּוֹעֶה מַה, יְתַקֵּן תֵּיכֶף בָּאוֹר.
and when one wanders, he rectifies immediately through the light.
וּמַאֲמַר "יְהִי אוֹר" נֶגֶד מִדַּת חָכְמָה.
And the utterance 'Let there be light' corresponds to the attribute of Chokhmah.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּנֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, וּנְשָׁמָה מִשְׁכָּנָם בְּמוֹחַ, לֵב, וְכָבֵד;
And it is known that Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah reside in brain, heart, and liver;
וְהַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ אֵינָהּ נִפְגֶּמֶת כְּלָל,
and the Neshamah in the brain is not blemished at all,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה הִיא",
as is stated: 'The soul You gave within me is pure,'
וּכְשֶׁפּוֹגֵם – מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת הַנְּשָׁמָה.
and when one blemishes, the Neshamah departs.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַאֲמָר ג': "וִיהִי מַבְדִּיל בֵּין מַיִם לָמָיִם",
And afterward the third utterance: 'and let it divide the waters from the waters,'
נֶגֶד מִדַּת בִּינָה – לִבָּא.
corresponds to the attribute of Binah—the heart.
וְכֵן בָּאָדָם הָרוּחַ שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
And so within man, the Ruach which resides in the heart,
שָׁם יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי חַלְלֵי הַלֵּב:
there exist the two cavities of the heart: "
לֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ וְלֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ",
'a wise man's heart is at his right, but a fool's heart at his left,'
וְזֶה עִיקַּר הַמִּלְחָמָה,
and this is the primary arena of battle,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרָכוֹת ה.):
as stated (Berakhot 5a): "
לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע".
"A person should always stir up the good inclination against the evil inclination."
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל מַחֲלוֹקֶת,
And since division/strife commenced,
לֹא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "כִּי טוֹב" בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי,
it was not said on it 'that it was good' on the second day,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּבְרָא בוֹ אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם (פְּסָחִים נד.);
because the fire of Gehenna was created upon it (Pesachim 54a);
דְּגֵיהִנָּם נִבְרָא קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם,
for Gehenna itself was created before the world was created,
רַק אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם נִבְרָא בַּשֵּׁנִי.
only the fire of Gehenna was created on Monday.
וּכְתִיב: "וְאִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה",
And it is written: 'and their fire shall not be quenched,'
וְלֹא כְתִיב "וְאֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם", רַק "וְאִשָּׁם",
and it is not written 'and the fire of Gehenna', but 'their fire',
וְהַיְינוּ נוּרָא דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁהוּא אֵשׁ,
namely the fire of the evil inclination, which is burning fire,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (קִדּוּשִׁין פא.):
as stated (Kiddushin 81a): "
נָפֵיק מִינֵיהּ כִּי עַמּוּדָא דְּנוּרָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי דְּאַתְּ נוּרָא";
"It emerged from him like a pillar of fire; he said to it: See that you are fire!"
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ (יוֹמָא סט:):
and so we find (Yoma 69b): "
נָפֵיק אֲתָא כִּי גוּרְיָא דְּנוּרָא מִבֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, אֲמַר לֵיהּ נָבִיא: הַיְינוּ יִצְרָא וְכוּלֵי זֹאת הָרִשְׁעָה".
"It came forth like a fiery cub from the Holy of Holies; the prophet said: This is the inclination, etc., this is Wickedness."
וְאִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ ט, ח):
And it is brought (Bereishit Rabbah, this parashah 9:8): "
לֹא יוֹם וְלֹא גֵּיהִנָּם,
"'There is neither day nor Gehenna,
אֶלָּא אֵשׁ יוֹצְאָה מִגּוּפָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים וּמְלַהֲטָתוֹ,
rather a fire emerges from the body of the wicked and consumes him,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'רוּחֲכֶם אֵשׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶם'".
as it is said: "Your breath, as fire, shall devour you."'
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִזְכַּר בִּבְרִיאַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע "טוֹב",
And since 'good' is not mentioned regarding the creation of the evil inclination,
הוּא רַע,
it is defined as evil,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שַׁבָּת קמט:):
as stated (Shabbat 149b): "
כָּל שֶׁחֲבֵירוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
"'Anyone whose fellow is punished through him...'
דִּכְתִיב: 'גַּם עֲנוֹשׁ לַצַּדִּיק לֹא טוֹב',
for it is written: 'To punish the righteous is also not good,'
וְאֵין 'לֹא טוֹב' אֶלָּא רַע",
and 'not good' means nothing other than evil,'
וּכְתִיב: "לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע",
and it is written: 'evil shall not dwell with You,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (סֻכָּה נב.): "הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קְרָאוֹ רַע".
and as stated (Sukkah 52a): 'The Holy One called it evil.'
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וּבוֹרֵא רָע"
– And this is what is meant by 'and Creator of evil'—
שֶׁבָּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁנִּקְרָא רַע.
that He created the evil inclination which is termed evil.
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה אָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה טו.):
And opposite this they said (Chagigah 15a): "
בָּרָא צַדִּיקִים, בָּרָא רְשָׁעִים, בָּרָא גַּן עֵדֶן, בָּרָא גֵּיהִנָּם";
"He created righteous ones, He created wicked ones, He created Gan Eden, He created Gehenna";
לֹא אָמַר כָּאן "מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים", רַק "רְשָׁעִים",
he did not say here 'the deeds of the wicked,' but 'wicked ones',
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בְּרִיאַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע יוּכַל לִטְעוֹת בְּמַעֲשֵׂה רֶשַׁע מַמָּשׁ.
for through the creation of the evil inclination one may stumble into actual wicked deeds.
אַךְ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "הַמְשֵׁל וָפַחַד עִמּוֹ",
Yet from the perspective of Hashem: 'Dominion and fear are with Him,'
וְדָרְשׁוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, יב עַמּוּד ב):
and they expounded in the holy Zohar (Part III, 12b): "
הַמְשֵׁל – דָּא מִיכָאֵל, וּפַחַד – דָּא גַּבְרִיאֵל;
'Dominion—this is Michael; and fear—this is Gabriel;
דָּא יְסוֹדָא דִּילֵיהּ מִמַּיָּא, וְדָא יְסוֹדָא דִּילֵיהּ מֵאֶשָׁא,
the foundation of this one is of water, and the foundation of that one is of fire,
וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עָבֵיד שְׁלָמָא בֵּינַיְיהוּ וְכוּלֵי";
and the Holy One makes peace between them, etc.';
רַק מִצַּד הָאָדָם הוּא עִיקַּר הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת,
only from man's perspective does primary discord arise,
וְהוּא הֵיפֶךְ שֶׁל הַשָּׁלוֹם,
and it is the antithesis of peace,
וְזֶהוּ "עוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם וּבוֹרֵא רָע".
and this is 'Maker of peace and Creator of evil.'
וּבָזֶה לֹא נִזְכַּר "כִּי טוֹב",
And within this 'that it was good' is not mentioned,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל הַמִּלְחָמָה וְהַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת.
since warfare and strife began.
וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ד, ו):
And they said (Bereishit Rabbah 4:6): "
וּמַה מַּחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁהוּא לְקִיּוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם לֹא נֶאֱמַר בָּהּ כִּי טוֹב",
"'And if concerning a division which is for the preservation of the world it was not said "that it was good"',"
שֶׁנִּבְרָא רָקִיעַ לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין מַיִם לָמָיִם,
for the firmament was created to divide between waters and waters,
וְהַיְינוּ בֵּין גּוּף לַנֶּפֶשׁ,
meaning between body and soul,
דְּהַגּוּף נִקְרָא אֶרֶץ,
since the physical body is termed 'earth',
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא:):
as is stated (Sanhedrin 91b): "'
יִקְרָא אֶל הַשָּׁמַיִם מֵעָל' – זוֹ נְשָׁמָה, 'וְאֶל הָאָרֶץ' – זֶה הַגּוּף".
"'He calls to the heavens above'—this is the soul; 'and to the earth'—this is the body."
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַכֹּל אֶחָד: "עוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו".
However from the side of Hashem everything is one: 'He makes peace in His heights.'
וְהָרָע לֹא נִבְרָא רַק כְּדֵי לְמַתְּקוֹ,
And evil was created solely in order to sweeten it,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ).
as stated (in Tanchuma, this parashah).
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בְּתוֹסָפוֹת לְפָרָשַׁת בָּלָק דַּף רו עַמּוּד ב):
And in the holy Zohar (in additions to Parashat Balak, 206b):
פָּתַח רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: "'מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ בְעֵינַי נִכְבַּדְתָּ' וְכוּלֵי,
Rabbi Eleazar opened: "'Since you were precious in My sight, you have been honored, etc.'
דְּכָל בַּר נָשׁ דְּאִיהוּ בְּחוֹבָא קַמֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא אִיהוּ מְזַלְזְלָא וְכוּלֵי,
for any man who abides in sin before the Holy One is debased, etc.,
וּבָתַר דְּאִמְלַךְ וְתָב מֵחוֹבֵיהּ,
and after he reconsiders and turns from his sin,
הַשְׁתָּא אִיהוּ דְּאִתְיַקַּר מִגַּרְמֵיהּ,
now he has become precious through his own effort,
וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא קָארֵי עֲלֵיהּ: 'מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ בְעֵינַי נִכְבַּדְתָּ' וְכוּלֵי",
and the Holy One calls regarding him: "Since you were precious in My sight, you have been honored, etc.",
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה הוּא נַעֲשָׂה טוֹב מְאֹד.
meaning that afterward through repentance he becomes 'very good.'
וּכְמָשָׁל הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב מִבֶּן מֶלֶךְ שֶׁנִּפְדָּה מִשִּׁבְיָה,
And like the parable of the Baal Shem Tov concerning a prince redeemed from captivity,
שֶׁהוּא חָשׁוּב יוֹתֵר לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ מֵהַבֵּן הַיּוֹשֵׁב אֶצְלוֹ תָּדִיר;
who is more precious before the king than the prince who resides beside him constantly;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לד:): "לְרָחוֹק וַהֲדַר לְקָרוֹב".
and as they said (Berakhot 34b): 'to the far, and then to the near.' "
וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ"
– 'And I have loved you'—
דְּלֵית לֵיהּ רְחִימוּ לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בַּהֲדֵי בַּר נָשׁ בְּהַאי עָלְמָא אֶלָּא בְּמַאן דְּתָב מֵחוֹבֵיהּ,
for the Holy One has no such love for any person in this world except for one who repents of his sin,
וְעַל דָּא "וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ".
and regarding this: 'and I have loved you.'

And this is because he is drawn with extra strength,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קכט עַמּוּד ב).
as stated (Zohar Part I, 129b).
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "עוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם וּבוֹרֵא רָע",
And upon this they stated: 'Maker of peace and Creator of evil,'
וְהוּא הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁהוּא לְקִיּוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְיִשּׁוּבוֹ שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי.
this being the division which serves the preservation of the world and its settlement, created on the second day.
וּבָתַר דְּתָב מֵחוֹבֵיהּ עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ טוֹב,
And after one repents of his sin He makes it good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּתַּנְחוּמָא שֶׁבָּרָא הָרַע לְמַתְּקוֹ.
as stated in Tanchuma, that He created the evil to sweeten it.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נד.):
And regarding this they taught (Pesachim 54a):
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "כִּי טוֹב", חָזַר וּכְלָלוֹ בַּשִּׁשִּׁי,
even though 'that it was good' was not said of it, He integrated it on the sixth day,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיַּרְא וְגוֹמֵר אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד",
as it is said: 'And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good,'
שֶׁמִּכָּל הַהֵיפֶךְ יִצְמַח שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹב מְאֹד.
in that from every opposite will sprout forth that which is very good.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, קפד עַמּוּד א):
And as stated in the holy Zohar (Part II, 184a): "
דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא, וְלֵית טָבָא וְכוּלֵי".
"there is no light except that which emerges from darkness, nor good, etc."
וְזֶה שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה: "וּבוֹרֵא אֶת הַכֹּל"
– And this is why the Men of the Great Assembly formulated: 'and Creator of all'—
לִישָׁנָא מְעַלְּיָא,
an exalted, euphemistic expression,
דְּ"כֹל" רוֹמֵז עַל הַהֵיפֶךְ מֵהַטּוֹב.
for 'all' alludes to the opposite of the good.
וּבְשַׁבָּת, דְּאִיתָא: "כָּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ" (שַׁבָּת קיח:),
And on Shabbat, concerning which it is brought: 'Whoever delights in Shabbat is given the desires of his heart' (Shabbat 118b),
וְלֹא אָמַר "לְטוֹבָה",
and it did not specify 'for good',
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם בְּשַׁבָּת לְטוֹבָה,
because all desires of a person on Shabbat are inherently for good,
דִּכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת עָדִיף מֵאֶלֶף תַּעֲנִיּוֹת (תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ).
for the honor of Shabbat surpasses a thousand fasts (Tanchuma, this parashah).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח:):
And this is what they said in the Gemara (Shabbat 118b): "
כָּל הַמְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת כְּהִלְכָתוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּדוֹר אֱנוֹשׁ – מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ".
"Whoever observes Shabbat according to its halakhah, even if he served idolatry like the generation of Enosh—he is forgiven."
וַהֲרֵי חָשְׁבוּ (יוֹמָא פו.) אַרְבַּע חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה,
And behold, they enumerated (Yoma 86a) four categories of atonement,
וַחֲמוּרוֹת – שֶׁתְּשׁוּבָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים תּוֹלִין וְיִסּוּרִין מְמָרְקִין;
and for severe transgressions—repentance and Yom Kippur suspend and afflictions cleanse;
וְעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּדוֹר אֱנוֹשׁ יֵשׁ בּוֹ חִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם,
and one who serves idolatry like the generation of Enosh commits a desecration of the Name,
שֶׁרַק מִיתָה מְמָרֶקֶת!
which only death cleanses!
רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּעַנֵּג הַשַּׁבָּת לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
Yet through delighting in Shabbat for the sake of Heaven,
עָדִיף מֵאֶלֶף תַּעֲנִיּוֹת.
it is superior to a thousand fasts.
וּבְתִקּוּנֵי תְּשׁוּבָה נִזְכְּרוּ תַּעֲנִיּוֹת לְכָל חֵטְא,
And in penitential regimens fasts are specified for every sin,
וְהוּא לְהָגֵן מֵהַיִּסּוּרִין עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ יִסּוּרִין,
this being to shield oneself from afflictions by willingly taking afflictions upon oneself,
וְכָתַב סֵדֶר תַּעֲנִיּוֹת וּמִסְפָּרָם לְכָל חֵטְא;
recording the arrangement of fasts and their precise number for each transgression;
וְעַל יְדֵי כְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת מְתַקֵּן הַכֹּל,
and through the honor of Shabbat he rectifies all,
וּמוֹחֲלִין לוֹ אֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּדוֹר אֱנוֹשׁ,
and he is forgiven even if he served idolatry like the generation of Enosh,
וְנוֹתְנִין לוֹ כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ,
and they grant him all the desires of his heart,
שֶׁהַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה.
for everything is for good.
וְלָכֵן בִּיצִיאַת שַׁבָּת אָנוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין:
Therefore at the conclusion of Shabbat we pray: "
יָשִׂים עָלֵינוּ בְּרָכָה וְשָׁלוֹם".
'May He place upon us blessing and peace.'

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 2:5: “Rabbi Abahu and Rabbi Ḥiyya the Great, Rabbi Abahu said: Right from the beginning of the creation of the world, the Holy One blessed be He foresaw the actions of the righteous and the actions of the wicked. That is what is written: “For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish” (Psalms 1:6). “The earth was emptiness and disorder” – these are the actions of the wicked. “God said: Let there be light” – these are the actions of the righteous. But I do not know which He desires, whether it is the actions of these, or the actions of those. When it is written: “God saw the light, that it was good” (Genesis 1:4) – this shows that He desires the actions of the righteous, and does not desire the actions of the wicked. Rabbi Ḥiyya the Great said: Right from the beginning of the creation of the world, the Holy One blessed be He foresaw the Temple built, destroyed, and rebuilt. “In the beginning God created [the heavens and the earth]” – that indicates [the Temple] being built, as it says: “To plant the heavens and to lay the foundation of the earth and to say to Zion: You are My people” (Isaiah 51:16). “The earth was emptiness and disorder” – that indicates [the Temple] destroyed, just as it says: “I have seen the land, and behold, it is emptiness and disorder” (Jeremiah 4:23). “God said: Let there be light” – that indicates [the Temple] being built and perfected in the future, as it says: “Arise, shine, for your light has come” (Isaiah 60:1), and it is written: “For, behold, the darkness will cover the earth, and nations, a fog; but upon you the Lord will shine and His glory will be seen upon you” (Isaiah 60:2).”

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 5a:2: “Incidental to the verse, “Tremble, and do not sin,” the Gemara mentions that Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: One should always incite his good inclination against his evil inclination, i.e., that one must constantly struggle so that his evil inclination does not lead him to transgression, as it is stated: "Tremble, and do not sin." If one succeeds and subdues his evil inclination, excellent, but if he does not succeed in subduing it, he should study Torah, as alluded to in the verse: “Say to your heart.” If he subdues his evil inclination, excellent; if not, he should recite Shema, which contains the acceptance of the yoke of God, and the concept of reward and punishment, as it is stated in the verse: “Upon your bed,” which alludes to Shema, where it says: “When you lie down.” If he subdues his evil inclination, excellent; if not, he should remind himself of the day of death, whose silence is alluded to in the continuation of the verse: “And be still, Selah.””

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 54a:13: “The Gemara asks: And was its fire created on Shabbat eve? Wasn’t it taught in a baraita that Rabbi Yosei says: The fire that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created on the second day of the week will never be extinguished, as it is stated: “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcasses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm shall not die, nor will their fire be extinguished; and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh” (Isaiah 66:24)? And Rabbi Bana’a, son of Rabbi Ulla, said: Why doesn’t the verse state: That it was good, at the end of the second day of the week of Creation, as it does on the other days? It is because on that day the fire of Gehenna was created. And Rabbi Elazar said that even though: That it was good, was not stated with regard to the creations of the second day, He later included it on the sixth day, as it is stated: “And God saw all that He had done and behold, it was very good” (Genesis 1:31).”

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 81a:12: “When he was halfway up the ladder, he strengthened his legs against the sides of the ladder to stop himself from climbing further, raised his voice, and cried out: There is a fire in the house of Amram. Upon hearing this, the Sages came and found him in that position. They said to him: You have embarrassed us, since everyone sees what you had intended to do. Rav Amram said to them: It is better that you be shamed in Amram’s house in this world, and not be ashamed of him in the World-to-Come. He took an oath that his evil inclination should emerge from him, and an apparition similar to a pillar of fire emerged from him. He said to his evil inclination: See, as you are fire and I am mere flesh, and yet, I am still superior to you, as I was able to overcome you.”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 69b: ‘In response to the indication of divine acceptance, they observed a fast for three days and three nights, and He delivered the evil inclination to them. A form of a fiery lion cub came forth from the chamber of the Holy of Holies. Zechariah the prophet said to the Jewish people: This is the evil inclination for idol worship, as it is stated in the verse that refers to this event: “And he said: This is the evil one” (Zechariah 5:8). The use of the word “this” indicates that the evil inclination was perceived in a physical form.’

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 4:6: ““God made the firmament, and divided between the water that was under the firmament and the water that was above the firmament; and it was so” (Genesis 1:7). “God made the firmament” – this is one of the verses due to which ben Zoma stirred up commotion in the world. “[God] made”? This is bewildering; for were they not [brought about] by God’s mere word? That is, “By the word of the Lord were the heavens made; by the breath of His mouth, all their hosts” (Psalms 33:6). Why is “that it was good” not written regarding the second day? Rabbi Yoḥanan taught it in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Ḥalafta: It is because Gehenna was created on it, as it is stated: “For the inferno is arranged from yesterday” (Isaiah 30:33) – a day that has a yesterday, but does not have a day before yesterday. Rabbi Ḥanina says: It is because division was created, as it is stated: “And let it divide between water and water.” Rabbi Tavyomei said: If on account of division that is for the improvement of the world and its settlement, there is no “that it was good,” division that causes turmoil in the world, all the more so. Rabbi Shmuel [bar Naḥman] said: It is because the work of creating water was not completed. That is why “that it was good” is written twice on the third day; once for the work of creating the water, and once for the other work done on that day. A certain noblewoman asked Rabbi Yosei, saying to him: ‘Why is “that it was good” not written regarding the second day?’ He said to her: ‘Nevertheless, it ultimately returned and included everything at the end, as it is stated: “God saw everything that He had made, and, behold, it was very good”’ (Genesis 1:31). She said to him: ‘This is analogous to six people who come to you and you give each one of them a maneh, but to one of them you do not give a maneh. You then give one maneh for everyone [to be divided among them] – will the result not be that they all have a maneh and a sixth in their hands, but one of them has only one sixth of a maneh in his hand?’ This was a rhetorical question. He then said to her in accordance with what Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: ‘It is because the work of creating water was not completed.’ That is why “that it was good” is written twice on the third day; once for the work of creating water, and once for the other work done on that day. Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai: It is written: “He tells the outcome from the outset” (Isaiah 46:10) – from the beginning of the creation of the world, the Holy One blessed be He foresaw that Moses would be called “good” (Exodus 2:2) and that he was destined to receive his [punishment] because of it [water]. That is why “that it was good” is not written regarding it. Rabbi Simon said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: This is analogous to a king who had a ruthless legion. The king said: ‘Since this legion is ruthless, let my name not be written in association with it.’ So, too, the Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Since the generation of the Flood, the generation of Enosh, and the generation of the Dispersion were all penalized by it [water], therefore, let “that it was good” not be written in association with it.’”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 118b:2: “Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: One who delights in Shabbat is rescued from the oppression of exile. He derives it by means of a verbal analogy. It is written here, with regard to Shabbat: “And I will cause you to ride on the heights [bamotei] of the world” (Isaiah 58:14), and it is written there: “You are fortunate Israel, who is like you? A nation redeemed by God, the shield that aids you and the sword of your triumph. Your enemies will try to defeat you and you will trample their high places [bamoteimo]” (Deuteronomy 33:29). Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: With regard to anyone who delights in the Shabbat, God grants him his heart’s desires, as it is stated: “And you shall delight in God and He will grant you your heart’s desires” (Psalms 37:4). This delight in God, which is mentioned in the verse, I do not know what it is. When it says: “And you shall call the Shabbat delight,” one must say: It is the delight of Shabbat. The Gemara asks: With what does one delight in the day of Shabbat? Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav: With a dish of beets, and large fish, and heads of garlic. Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said: Even with regard to a small item and one prepared it in deference to Shabbat, it is a delight. The Gemara asks: What is the small item mentioned? Rav Pappa said: Small fried fish.”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86a:7: “These are the categories: If one violates a positive mitzva and repents, he is forgiven even before he moves from his place, i.e. immediately, as it is stated: “Return, you backsliding children, I will heal your backsliding” (Jeremiah 3:22), implying that when one repents he is immediately forgiven. If one violates a prohibition and repents, repentance suspends his punishment and Yom Kippur atones for his sin, as it is stated: “For on this day shall atonement be made for you, to purify you from all your sins” (Leviticus 16:30). If one commits a transgression that warrants karet or a sin punishable by death from the earthly court and then repents, repentance and Yom Kippur suspend his punishment, and suffering absolves and completes the atonement, as it is stated: “Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with strokes” (Psalms 89:33).”

h: Motzaei Shabbat and the Sixfold Language of Salvation
Verses recited around Havdalah carry the blessing of Shabbat into the coming six days.
Six Expressions of Salvation at Havdalah

p: קוֹדֶם הַבְדָּלָה אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים פְּסוּקִים שֶׁל יְשׁוּעוֹת,
Prior to Havdalah we recite verses of salvations,
וּבָהֶם שֵׁשׁ פְּעָמִים לְשׁוֹן יְשׁוּעָה,
and within them six times the expression of salvation,
וְהַשִּׁשִּׁי: "כּוֹס יְשׁוּעוֹת אֶשָּׂא",
and the sixth: 'I will lift the cup of salvations,'
הַמְּרַמֵּז לִישׁוּעָה כְּפוּלָה,
which alludes to a double salvation,
שֶׁנִּכְלָל בּוֹ שְׁבִיעִית;
wherein a seventh is enfolded;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פח)
and as the Midrash alludes (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 88)
בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ שֶׁל שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים שֶׁנֶּזְכַּר אַרְבַּע פְּעָמִים כּוֹס,
in the dream of the chief butler wherein 'cup' is mentioned four times,
וְנֶגְדָּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁקֶה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אַרְבַּע כּוֹסוֹת לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא,
and parallel to them Hashem gives Israel to drink four cups in the World to Come,
וּמוֹנֶה שָׁם "כּוֹס יְשׁוּעוֹת אֶשָּׂא" לִשְׁנַיִם.
counting there 'I will lift the cup of salvations' as two.
וְהַשִּׁבְעָה יְשׁוּעוֹת הֵמָּה כְּעִנְיַן שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הֶחָג,
And the seven salvations reflect the seven days of the festival of Sukkot,
שֶׁאָנוּ שׁוֹאֲגִים בְּכָל יוֹם "הוֹשַׁע נָא",
wherein we cry out each day 'Hoshana',
וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי נִקְרָא הוֹשַׁעְנָא רַבָּה,
and the seventh day is called Hoshana Rabbah,
וְאָז הוּא זְמַן נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם,
and then is the time of the water libation,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּשְׁאַבְתֶּם מַיִם בְּשָׂשׂוֹן מִמַּעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה".
as it is said: 'And you shall draw water with joy from the fountains of salvation.'
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת מַיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים הַנִּקְרָאִים מַעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה,
Namely, the dimension of supernal waters which are termed the fountains of salvation;
דְּמַיִם הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים נִקְרָא הַתְּשׁוּקָה וְהַצִּפּוּי לִישׁוּעָה
for the lower waters represent the yearning and longing for salvation
בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּבִתְפִלָּה מִצַּד אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא,
in repentance and prayer from the aspect of the arousal from below,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שִׁפְכִי כַמַּיִם לִבֵּךְ וְגוֹמֵר".
as is stated: 'Pour out your heart like water, etc.'
וְהוּא בִּזְמַן אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם הָאַחֲרוֹנִים שֶׁנִּשְׁלְמוּ בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים;
And this unfolds during the final forty days culminating on Yom Kippur;
וּבְשִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הֶחָג זְמַן נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם,
and during the seven days of Sukkot is the time of the water libation,
שֶׁהוּא הַשְׁפָּעַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִלְּעֵילָּא בְּכָל שֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת,
which is the flow of holiness from Above into all seven holy emotional attributes,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מוֹצָאָם מִמְּקוֹר מַעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה.
that their emergence be from the source of the fountains of salvation.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּכָל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַשָּׁבוּעַ
And likewise throughout all seven days of the week,
מוֹפִיעַ קְדוּשַׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת עַל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
the holiness of the Sabbath day radiates upon the six working days
לְקַדֵּשׁ הַמִּדּוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
to sanctify the personal attributes that they reside in holiness.
וְעַל זֶה אָנוּ מַזְכִּירִים בְּצֵאת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת הַשֵּׁשׁ פְּעָמִים יְשׁוּעָה
And for this we mention at the departure of Shabbat six expressions of salvation,
וְנִכְלָלִים בָּהּ שִׁבְעָה,
and seven are enfolded within them,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּכָּלְלוּ כָּל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בִּקְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת הֶעָבָר,
so that all six working days be enfolded in the sanctity of the past Sabbath,
לְטַהֵר וּלְקַדֵּשׁ הַמִּדּוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מִמַּעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה.
to purify and sanctify the attributes that they emerge from the fountains of salvation.
וְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת חֶסֶד שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָׁה,
And Sunday, which corresponds to the holy attribute of Chesed,
צָרִיךְ יְשׁוּעָה לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁמָר מֵהַהִיפּוּךְ
requires salvation to be guarded from its opposite,
שֶׁהוּא "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה",
which is 'one corresponding to the other',
שֶׁהֵם הַשִּׁבְעָה שֵׁמוֹת שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע הַנִּזְכָּר בְּדִבְרֵי חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה נב.),
these being the seven names of the evil inclination mentioned in the words of our Sages (Sukkah 52a),
זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה כְּנֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
counterpoised to the seven holy attributes.
וְהַשֵּׁם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא "רַע"
And its first name, which the Holy One called it, is 'evil',
הוּא הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא רַע,
which is the inclination of lust termed evil,
כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת אַהֲבַת חֶסֶד שֶׁל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
counter to the lovingkindness of holy love.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּכָל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת
And likewise across all seven attributes,
נִצְרָךְ יְשׁוּעָה לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁמָר מִבְּחִינַת הַהֵיפֶךְ הַמְּנַגֵּד לַקְּדוּשָּׁה, זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה.
salvation is needed to be protected from the opposing force confronting holiness, one against the other.
וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה:
And this is the entire mission of man in this world:
לִהְיוֹת תָּמִיד מְצַפֶּה לִישׁוּעָה,
to be continually yearning for salvation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שַׁבָּת לא.):
as stated (Shabbat 31a):
שֶׁלֶּעָתִיד שׁוֹאֲלִים לָאָדָם "צִפִּיתָ לִישׁוּעָה?".
that in the ultimate future they ask a person: 'Did you yearn for salvation?'
וְעִיקַּר הָעֵצָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי קְבִיעוּת עִתִּים לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And the primary counsel is through setting fixed times for the Oral Torah,
וּבִפְרָט בַּלֵּילוֹת הָאֲרוּכִים שֶׁבִּתְקוּפַת טֵבֵת,
especially during the long nights of the winter season of Tevet,
דְּלָא אִיבְרֵי לַיְלָה אֶלָּא לְגִירְסָא,
for night was created solely for rigorous study,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (עֵירוּבִין סה. וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת).
as stated (Eruvin 65a and in Tosafot).
וְהַסֵּדֶר אַחַר שְׁאֵלַת "צִפִּיתָ לִישׁוּעָה":
And the order following the inquiry 'Did you yearn for salvation?' is: "
פִּלְפַּלְתָּ בְּחָכְמָה, הֵבַנְתָּ דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר".
'Did you analyze with wisdom? Did you understand one matter from within another?'

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 88:5: ““The chief butler related his dream to Joseph, and said to him: In my dream, behold, a vine was before me” (Genesis 40:9). “And on the vine were three tendrils, and it was as though it was budding; its blossoms emerged, and its clusters produced ripe grapes” (Genesis 40:10). “The chief butler related…behold, a vine was before me” – this is Israel, as it is stated: “You transported a vine from Egypt” (Psalms 80:9). “And on the vine were three tendrils” – Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. “It was as though it was budding” – the redemption of Israel was budding. “Its blossoms emerged” – the redemption of Israel blossomed. “Its clusters produced ripe grapes” – the vine that budded immediately blossomed; grapes that emerged immediately ripened. “And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; I took the grapes, pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand” (Genesis 40:11). “Joseph said to him: This is its interpretation: The three tendrils are three days” (Genesis 40:12). “In three more days Pharaoh will raise your head and restore you to your position, and you will give Pharaoh's cup into his hand, like the former circumstance where you would provide him with drink” (Genesis 40:13). “And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand” – on this basis the Sages instituted the four cups on Passover eve. Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Benaya: Corresponding to the four expressions of redemption that were stated in Egypt: “I will take you out…I will deliver you…I will redeem you…I will take you” (Exodus 6:6–7). Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: Corresponding to the four cups stated here: “And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand… you will give Pharaoh's cup into his hand…” Rabbi Levi said: Corresponding to the four kingdoms. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Corresponding to the four cups [kosot] of bewilderment that the Holy One blessed be He will give the idolaters to drink. That is what is written: “For so said the Lord, God of Israel, to me: Take this cup of the wine of anger” (Jeremiah 25:15); “a golden cup is Babylon in the hand of the Lord…” (Jeremiah 51:7); “he will rain…upon the wicked [ blazing coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their lot [menat kosam]]” (Psalms 11:6). Corresponding to them, the Holy One blessed be He will give Israel four cups [kosot] of salvation in the future, as it is stated: “The Lord is my lot [menat kosi]” (Psalms 16:5); “I will lift a cup of salvation [kos yeshuot]” (Psalms 116:13): “You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup is full” (Psalms 23:5). “A cup of salvation [kos yeshua]” (Psalms 116:13) is not written here, but rather, “a cup of salvation [kos yeshuot]” – one for the messianic era and one for the days of Gog. “If only you remember me when it shall be well for you, and please, perform kindness with me and mention me to Pharaoh, and take me out of this house” (Genesis 40:14). [Joseph] said to him: ‘You gave me good tidings; I, too, will give you good tidings: “In three more days…if only you remember me…”’ “For I was abducted from the land of the Hebrews and here, too, I have done nothing, that they placed me in the pit” (Genesis 40:15). “For I was abducted [gunov gunavti]” – Rav Aḥa said: From here [it may be derived] that he was abducted twice. “And here, too, I have done [nothing]…””

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52a: ‘§ Rabbi Avira, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, taught: The evil inclination has seven names. The Holy One, Blessed be He, called it evil, as it is stated: “For the inclination of a man’s heart is evil from his youth” (Genesis 8:21). Moses called it uncircumcised, as it is stated: “And circumcise the foreskin of your hearts” (Deuteronomy 10:16). David called it impure, as it is stated: “Create for me a pure heart, O God” (Psalms 51:12); by inference, there is an impure heart that is the evil inclination.’

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 230:1: “Moshe our teacher subsequently mentioned only “wise men,” as they said (Eruvin 100b), that men of understanding were not found. It is known that binah is the heart, the perception within the heart; and it says, “Hashem has not given you a heart to know … until this day,” for they were redeemed only through faith. That is, although wise Torah scholars were found, as long as wisdom does not add perception to the heart, it comes only from the power of nefesh, the soul’s level of embodied action, for each of the soul’s levels itself includes nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah and yechidah, as is known. Wisdom that does not continually add fresh vitality to the heart is only the mitzvah of Torah study, like the performance of all the practical mitzvot, which belongs to nefesh alone, from the rooted faith that one must obey Hashem and engage in His mitzvot and Torah. This is only the level of “men of valor,” subduing their inclination.”
